title: Review-value queue and kill gate 6
description: The ranked review queue and kill gate 6 measurement. Ratified 2026-08-17 in C1, revised 2026-08-18 in C2 after the C1 lift bootstrap was found to deduplicate its own resample. 0.2.0 adds the point_in_ci guard, the surviving-resample count and the bootstrap median, closes split results to unknown keys, and makes three contradictions unrepresentable: an unmeasurable split with no reason, a measurable split still carrying one, and a point estimate outside its own interval reported as a verdict about the gate. Four design constraints are enforced by construction. Every claim carries the count it was measured over, because a queue that surfaces four observations and gets three right is not 75% precision unless the denominator is stated. Every verdict is a four-valued enum with a not-measurable state, because a verdict that can only be good news is not a verdict. An absent measurement carries its reason, because a silent null is a suppressed finding. And the script validates its own output against this schema before writing, so a violating receipt never reaches disk.

split_manifest_sha256.description: Digest of the split manifest. A re-split invalidates all numbers here.

conflict_definition.description: The definition of an actionable conflict, fixed before ranking, not changed after seeing results.

fixed_before_measuring.description: Attestation that the definition was not changed after seeing the lift result.

review_budget.description: The fixed review budget used for all lift comparisons. Chosen before results were seen.

deduplication.description: Episode deduplication: one observation per (station, satellite, revolution) episode.

key.description: The fields that define an episode.

sha256_duplicate_policy.description: What happens when two episodes share a waterfall SHA-256.

n_sha256_duplicates_in_corpus.description: Measured count of SHA-256 duplicates in the corpus. Zero means the dedup rule was untested by the data; the test suite covers it with a constructed case.

queue.description: The ranked queue. One entry per episode, sorted descending by score.

per_split_summaries.description: Corpus counts per split. Deliberately holds no gate 6 measurement: the same number in two places is a drift surface, and a reader cannot tell which copy is authoritative. The measurement lives once, in gate6.per_split.

n_test_decisive.description: Observations carrying a with-signal or without-signal label. The denominator for every conflict claim on this split.

n_queue_after_dedup.description: Queue length after episode deduplication, so the cost of duplicate control is visible rather than inferred.

n_episodes_deduplicated.description: Observations removed by episode deduplication. Nearly zero on this corpus, because pass episodes hold 1.004 observations each and only 8 of 2716 hold more than one. Reported as a count so an inert rule is not mistaken for an exercised one.

n_degraded_revolution.description: Observations whose TLE would not yield a revolution index. These merge into one group per (station, satellite), which widens the interval rather than narrowing it, so the degraded case fails safe.

n_at_bound_obs.description: Observations whose fitted offset sits at the search-window bound. A value at the edge of its own search window is a floor, not a measurement, so the count is reported wherever offsets are ranked.

verdict.description: Four states, decided by the interval rather than the point estimate. PASSED: the whole interval clears the threshold. FAILED: the whole interval sits below it. NOT_ESTABLISHED: the interval contains the threshold, whichever side the point estimate falls on. NOT_MEASURABLE: the split lacked the data, or the statistic failed its own consistency check.

replay.description: Active-selection replay of every ordering over the same resampled populations. The comparisons are paired: one draw produces one synthetic population and every ordering is scored on it before the next draw, because drawing separately per ordering would attribute the difference between two populations to the difference between two orderings.

n_degenerate_resamples.description: Draws containing no conflict, where every ordering finds zero and no comparison is defined. Counted rather than silently skipped, because dropping them conditions the interval.

diff_point.description: Conflicts found by the queue minus conflicts found by the baseline at the same budget. The tested statistic: defined in every draw including those where a baseline finds nothing, with a null of exactly 0.

ratio_point.description: The same comparison on a ratio scale, with a +0.5 continuity correction on both terms applied in every draw rather than only where the denominator is zero, so the estimator does not change between draws.

direction.description: Four states. baseline_better must be representable: a one-sided survival test is what left an ablation rule's DROP branch as dead code in Wave B.

survives_correction.description: Whether the Bonferroni-widened interval excludes the null in either direction. True for a corrected loss as well as a corrected win.

clustering.description: How much of the variance in the conflict indicator sits between groups rather than within them. This is what a grouped interval exists to absorb, so it is measured rather than assumed.

icc.description: One-way random-effects intra-class correlation. A negative value is a real result on small samples and means within-group variance exceeds between-group variance; it is reported as measured.

design_effect.description: 1 + (mean group size - 1) * max(ICC, 0). The factor by which a clustered variance exceeds the independence variance. Near 1 means this grouping buys nothing.

concentration_record.description: Entity-concentration control, so one noisy station cannot fill a reviewer's budget. Shares fixed in docs/C2_PREREGISTRATION.md before the effect on lift was measured.

bound.description: Whether this cap displaced anything. A cap is credited whenever it would have blocked an entry, even if another cap would have blocked it too, so a false here is a property of the data rather than of the order the caps are checked in.

budget_filled.description: False when the caps left the budget short, which changes what "at the same budget" means in the gate's wording and so cannot be left to inference.

binding.description: Whether any entry was displaced. False means the caps are inert on this split, reported as such rather than implied to have been exercised.

episode_key.description: Canonical string form of (ground_station, norad_cat_id, orbital_revolution).

reasons.description: Fixed vocabulary, kept identical to QUEUE_REASONS in code by a test. NO_REASON means the observation is ranked but triggers no conflict criterion. The two DISPLACED codes say where a reviewer meets the entry, not what is wrong with it, so they sit alongside any conflict reasons rather than replacing them.

displaced_by_cap.description: Which entity cap displaced this entry below the budget line, if any. The entry is retained: a displaced observation is still a real candidate and a silently dropped row is a suppressed finding.

within_budget.description: Whether this entry falls inside the review budget after capping.

is_conflict.description: True iff at least one actionable reason (not OFFSET_AT_BOUND, not NO_REASON) applies.

model_prob.description: Calibrated image_corridor probability. Null when the image is missing.

ensemble_uncertainty.description: Standard deviation of the image_corridor episode-bootstrap ensemble for this observation. Null when not available.

split_gate6_result.description: One split's gate 6 measurement. additionalProperties is false so a misspelled key cannot silently read as an absent measurement, which is how a null becomes indistinguishable from a value nobody computed.

allOf.description: An unmeasurable split states why, in prose, with the counts that made it unmeasurable. A bare false is a suppressed finding.
A measurable split carries its interval, its counts and no leftover reason. A verdict of NOT_MEASURABLE beside measurable true is a contradiction.
A point estimate outside its own interval is a defect in the statistic, not a finding about the queue. It cannot be reported as a verdict about the gate.

n_queue_examined.description: Count of observations inspected at budget. A null here means the split was not measurable.

n_random_conflicts.description: Expected actionable conflicts at budget under random ordering.

n_queue_conflicts.description: Actionable conflicts found by the queue at budget.

lift_point.description: n_queue_conflicts / n_random_conflicts. Values above 1.5 are the target.

lift_ci95.description: The interval the verdict was decided on. When two groupings are available this is their union, which is conservative in both directions, so a verdict cannot be obtained by preferring whichever grouping clears the threshold.

lift_ci95_episode.description: Interval from resampling pass episodes, (station, satellite, orbital revolution). The finer grouping, and nearly inert on this corpus: episodes hold 1.004 observations each, so there is no within-episode correlation for it to absorb.

lift_ci95_station.description: Interval from resampling ground stations. Stations nest episodes, so this subsumes the episode grouping. A receiver and its local-oscillator error belong to a station and persist across passes, which is the correlation the grouped interval was introduced to absorb. Null when no station grouping was supplied or it could not be measured, in which case station_interval_note says which.

governing_interval.description: Which interval decided the verdict. Named rather than implied, so a reader does not have to infer it from the numbers.

station_interval_note.description: Why the station interval is absent, when it is. An absent measurement carries its reason.

verdict_episode_only.description: The verdict the episode-grouped interval alone would have given. Reported so the effect of adopting the conservative grouping is visible, not so that the more favourable of the two can be quoted.

n_station_groups.description: Distinct ground stations resampled for the station interval.

replay_episode.description: Four-baseline replay with pass episodes as the resampling unit.

replay_station.description: The same replay with ground stations as the resampling unit, which subsumes the episode grouping.

oneOf.description: One conclusion per baseline, requiring both groupings to survive correction and agree. Where they disagree the comparison is not_established with both directions named, because a disagreement between two defensible groupings is a real state rather than a reason to pick one.

lost_to.description: Baselines that beat the queue under both groupings. Present so a loss is representable rather than absent by construction.

uncapped_reference.description: Lift on the queue before entity-concentration caps. A reference point for the price of diversity, explicitly not eligible to be the verdict, because the shipped queue is the capped one.

fifo_lift_over_random.description: FIFO ordering's own lift over random at the same budget, not the queue's ratio over FIFO. Named for what it holds: the 0.1.0 key was called lift_vs_fifo while computing this, which reads as the opposite quantity.

image_uncertainty_lift_over_random.description: Image-only uncertainty ordering's own lift over random at the same budget.

physics_only_lift_over_random.description: Physics-only ordering's own lift over random at the same budget. The physics arm is weak by measurement (marginal AUC 0.466 to 0.567), so a low value here is expected and is not evidence about the queue.

n_boot_effective.description: Resamples that produced a finite lift, out of n_boot. A percentile interval drawn from a handful of surviving draws is not an interval, so the survivor count is reported next to it.

bootstrap_median.description: Median of the bootstrap distribution. Reported so the bias of the point estimate against its own resample is auditable rather than taken on trust.

point_in_ci.description: Whether the point estimate falls inside its own 95% interval, within percentile tolerance. Null means no interval existed to check, which is not the same as a check that passed. False means the resample and the point estimate are measuring different quantities. In C1 this was false on all four splits, because the resample deduplicated drawn episodes and so shrank the population by about a third while the budget stayed fixed, which drove lift to 1.0 by construction.

consistency_note.description: Present when point_in_ci is false. States both numbers and the gap between them.

verdict.description: PASSED: interval lo > 1.5. FAILED: interval hi < 1.5, the only shape that refutes the gate. NOT_ESTABLISHED: the interval contains 1.5, whichever side the point estimate falls on. NOT_MEASURABLE: no denominator, too few surviving resamples, or a point estimate outside its own interval.

n_groups.description: Number of pass episodes used for bootstrap resampling. Episodes, never observations: four captures of one pass share a receiver, a local-oscillator error and a sky geometry.
